questions.questionText: hour Additional Materials: Multiple Choice Answer Sheet Soft clean eraser Soft pencil (type B or HB is recommended) READ THESE INSTRUCTIONS FIRST Write in soft pencil. Do not use staples, paper clips, highlighters, glue or correction fluid. Write your name, Centre number and candidate number on the Answer Sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the separate Answer Sheet. Read the instructions on the Answer Sheet very carefully. Each correct answer will score one mark. A mark will not be deducted for a wrong answer. Any rough working should be done in this booklet.
A worker can make 10 hats or 5 pairs of shoes in a day. In the market three hats can be sold at the same price as two pairs of shoes. The worker should make

options.A: 4 hats and 3 pairs of shoes daily.
options.B: 6 hats and 2 pairs of shoes daily.
options.C: hats only.

questions.questionText: The table shows the market supply for a raw material and the individual demand of the three firms, X, Y and Z, which are its only buyers. price market demand demand demand $ supply by X by Y by Z (per kilo) (000s) (000s) (000s) (000s)
60 10 20 15 What is the equilibrium market price of the raw material?
In 2008 the demand curve for new cars in the European Union shifted to the left. Which change could have caused such a shift?

options.A: an increase in real disposable income
options.B: an increase in the cost of borrowing
options.C: an increase in the price of new cars
options.D: an increase in the price of train travel

questions.questionText: Worldwide, the film industry has increased its expenditure to over $1 billion each year on successful anti-piracy measures which it finances by charges on DVD products. How would this be shown in a demand and supply diagram of the market for legally produced DVDs? demand curve supply curve

options.A: shifts left shifts left
options.C: shifts right shifts left

questions.questionText: The demand for a commodity has unitary price elasticity. Which diagram shows the relationship between total expenditure on the commodity and its price?

options.A: B total total expenditure expenditure O O price price
options.C: D total total expenditure expenditure O O price price

questions.questionText: What does not happen when price acts as a means to allocate resources?

options.A: Price determines the supply of public goods.
options.B: Price operates in the markets for both goods and factors of production.
options.C: Price recognises consumers’ ability to pay rather than consumers’ needs.
options.D: Price signals to producers which goods are most profitable.

questions.questionText: James grows fruit trees in his garden. They attract butterflies and bees. What is not an externality of this?

options.A: Neighbours may be stung by the bees that pollinate the trees.
options.B: Neighbours may buy fruit more cheaply from James than the local supermarket.
options.C: Neighbours may enjoy better air quality as the trees naturally improve the atmosphere.
options.D: Neighbours may like to watch the activity of the wildlife at no cost.

questions.questionText: The table shows some of the costs when a firm produces a good. total cost to society external cost output $ $
322 18 What is the additional cost to a firm of producing the 24th unit?
What makes it particularly difficult to take decisions using cost-benefit analysis?

options.A: External costs are difficult to estimate accurately.
options.B: Governments have no method of valuing time savings.
options.C: Market forces have no influence on the outcome.
options.D: Private costs can vary from one day to the next.

questions.questionText: Which good is excludable but non-rival?

options.A: air defence
options.C: street lighting

questions.questionText: The diagram shows the demand and supply curves of a good. S price J D O quantity The government sets a maximum price of OJ for the good. How will this affect the consumers and producers of the good? effect on consumers effect on producers

options.A: All consumers will gain. Producers will lose.
options.B: All consumers will gain. Producers will gain.
options.C: Some consumers will gain and some will lose. Producers will gain.
options.D: Some consumers will gain and some will lose. Producers will lose.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows production possibility curves for two countries, X and Y. country Y good L country X O good M What can be deduced from the diagram?

options.A: Both countries can benefit from specialisation.
options.B: Country X has a higher opportunity cost than Y in producing good M.
options.C: Country Y has a comparative advantage in both goods.
options.D: Trade between X and Y will not take place.

questions.questionText: The statements that follow relate to possible gains from an increase in free trade. Which gain is least certain to result?

options.A: Increased specialisation leads to improvements in productivity.
options.B: Trade extends the choice of goods available to consumers.
options.C: Trade leads to an increase in the number of jobs.
options.D: Trade leads to a reduction in costs of production.

questions.questionText: A group of countries decides to change from being a customs union to being an economic union. What additional feature will this give the group?

options.A: a common external quota on imports from non-members
options.B: a common external tariff on imports from non-members
options.C: the removal of restrictions on the movement of capital and labour between members
options.D: the removal of tariffs and quotas on products exchanged between members

questions.questionText: The table shows the balance in $ million for four items in a country’s current account for two years. visibles invisibles income transfers Year 1 –72 84 –3 –24 Year 2 –87 96 12 –44 What can be concluded about the changes between Year 1 and Year 2?

options.A: Income has moved from a net inflow to a net outflow.
options.B: The difference between the value of exported and imported services has increased.
options.C: The value of exported goods has fallen.
options.D: Transfers into the country have increased.

questions.questionText: The diagram shows changes in the numbers employed in four different industries in a city between 2002 and 2007. finance manufacturing employment (000s) education leisure 2002 2003 2004 2005 2006 2007 What can be concluded from the diagram?

options.A: Finance was always the largest employer.
options.B: Leisure had the fastest growth rate in employment.
options.C: Manufacturing was the only industry to show signs of decline.
options.D: Total employment in the four industries decreased over the period.

questions.questionText: The average consumer divides his expenditure between food, accommodation and clothing in the ratio 5:3:2. During the course of a year, the price of food rises by 10%, the price of accommodation remains constant and the price of clothing falls by 5%. What is the increase in the Consumer Price Index over the year?
When is a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments likely to worsen?

options.A: when the government adopts a deflationary macroeconomic policy
options.B: when the government devalues the currency
options.C: when the prices of imported products that are demand-inelastic increase significantly
options.D: when tariffs are placed on imported products that are demand-elastic

questions.questionText: What would identify a country with a balance of payments disequilibrium?

options.A: alternate annual deficits and surpluses in the current account
options.C: a large short-term outflow of foreign direct investment
options.D: a persistent rise in foreign currency reserves

questions.questionText: The table shows the number of Jamaican dollars which exchanged for one unit of other currencies in June and July 2001. Jamaican $ Jamaican $ June 2001 July 2001 US$ 45.78 45.77 UK£ 63.86 64.37 Guyana $ 0.25 0.25 Barbados $ 23.19 23.12 What might be concluded from the table?

options.A: There was an increased demand for US$ by Jamaicans.
options.B: There was an increased supply of UK£ to Jamaicans.
options.C: There was a reduced supply of Guyana $ to Jamaicans.
options.D: There was a reduced demand for Barbados $ by Jamaicans.

questions.questionText: Following a long period of depreciation of the US$, both the US and UK monetary authorities raised their domestic interest rate. What will happen to the value of the exchange rate of the US$ in terms of UK£?

options.A: It will remain unchanged.
options.C: It will rise.

questions.questionText: In a command economy, what is the basis for determining the allocation of factors of production?

options.A: the pattern of consumers’ spending
options.B: the perceived needs of the country
options.C: the revenue from taxes
options.D: the size of public sector companies

options.A: Future growth prospects have been harmed.
options.B: The level of unemployment has fallen.
options.C: The opportunity cost of consumer goods has risen.
